meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/1919 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 October 2016 on legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
Due to the nature of this provision, implementation was not considered necessary. It is important to note, however, that while this is the official position, with respect to other (relevant) provisions of the Directive, the Dutch legislator points to existing legislation which in its view implements the Directive. It is therefore questionable whether it is accurate to say that the provision has not been implemented (due to its nature). Nevertheless, we have chosen to adopt the official position in this regard, thereby stressing that for a fuller picture of the degree of implementation of this provision in the Netherlands, the remainder of this transposition table should be consulted.


As a general preliminary remark, please note that the Directive was implemented entirely through existing legislation, as apparent from the official notification of implementation of the Dutch Government published on 20 October 2017, titled Mededeling van de implementatie van richtlijn (EU) 2016/1919 van het Europees parlement en de Raad van 26 oktober 2016 betreffende rechtsbijstand voor verdachten en beklaagden in strafprocedures en voor gezochte personen in procedures ter uitvoering van een Europees aanhoudingsbevel (PbEU 2016, L 297 (Staatscourant 2017, 59575), publicly available on zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl) and the accompanying transposition table. In the transposition table, the Government does not provide any further explanation as to how the existing legislation in question covers the relevant provision of the Directive (as it does do, for example, for Directive 2016/343); apparently, the Government deems this to be self-explanatory. In filling in this transposition table, the starting point was the official position with respect to the Directive's implementation, as set out in the transposition table accompanying the official notification. Where necessary, we have nuanced this position.


For a general overview of the Dutch legal aid system, the user is referred to the following brochure issued by the Dutch Legal Aid Board, dating from May 2019: https://www.rvr.org/binaries/content/assets/rvrorg/nieuws/2019/legal-aid-in-the-netherlands-a-broad-outline-may-2019.pdf.


Also worth mentioning here is that since 2013, successive governments have called for far-reaching changes and cuts to be made to the legal aid system, which has led to ongoing, critical debate. The most recent call for change was made in 2018, with the Dutch Bar Association taking the stance that the proposals are unnecessary, will lead to more bureaucracy and will make it more difficult for those with the lowest of incomes to access justice. To date, the question of how this all relates to the Directive has not featured prominently in this discussion, however, although it is clear that the criticisms made have the potential to raise issues under Article 7 of the Directive, in particular, regarding the quality of legal aid services.


Note that the term 'suspect' in this table may refer to the suspect or the accused, or both, depending on the context. This corresponds to the Dutch legal terminology, in which persons suspected of a crime are called 'suspects', both before and after indictment. Also worth noting here, is that the term '(recht op) rechtsbijstand' covers not only (the right to) legal aid, but also (the right to) legal assistance.

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning the right to legal aid for:

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: See the comments made above, with respect to Article 1 of the Directive.

items.text: (a)suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings; and

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: See the comments made above, with respect to Article 1 of the Directive.

items.text: (b)persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (requested persons).

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 2. This Directive complements Directives 2013/48/EU and (EU) 2016/800. Nothing in this Directive shall be interpreted as limiting the rights provided for in those Directives.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: (c)required or permitted to attend an investigative or evidence-gathering act, including as a minimum the following:

items.text: For the purposes of this Directive, ‘legal aid’ means funding by a Member State of the assistance of a lawyer, enabling the exercise of the right of access to a lawyer.

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons who lack sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer have the right to legal aid when the interests of justice so require.

provisions.textEn: Legal aid shall only be granted in respect of legal interests laying in the Dutch legal sphere, to natural or legal persons whose financial capacity does not exceed the amounts set out in Article 34.

Legal aid shall not be granted if:

a. the request for legal aid is evidently devoid of any foundation;

b. the costs related to the legal aid to be granted are not reasonably proportionate to the significance of the case;

c. the request for legal aid relates to a criminal case and it is likely, given the norm to have been violated, that a small fine relative the income will be imposed;

[…]

1. Legal aid as per the provisions of this statute shall be granted to those whose annual income is 21800 Euros [as of 1 January 2020: 27900 Euros] or less if they are a single householder, or, if they share a household with one or more persons, does not exceed 31000 Euros [as of 1 January 2020: 39400 Euros].
  2. In derogation of the provisions of paragraph 1 legal aid shall not be granted, where the litigant's assets exceed their tax-free allowance.
  3. Save in case of mutually contradictory interests, in determining the litigant's income and assets, consideration shall also be given to the income and assets of: (a) the spouse of registered partner of the litigant, unless at the time of the request they are permanently separated; (b) the person of the opposite or same sex with whom the litigant shares a household on a long-term basis, unless at the time of the request there exists between this person and the litigant a blood relationship of the first or second degree.
  4. The income limits as per the first paragraph shall be adjusted each year as of 1 January according to the percentage with which the salary index as of 31 October of the previous year deviates from the corresponding index as of 31 October of the year before that, on the understanding that this shall be rounded off to the nearest multiple of 100 Euros. Each year our Minister shall publish the indexed amounts in the Government Gazette [Staatscourant]. What the salary index, as per the first sentence, comprises, shall be set out in a Legislative Decree.

1. The litigant's income is the income data for the reference year. Insofar as there is no income data available for the litigant, income shall be understood to mean the amount that in the reference year approaches the income as best as possible, or the amount of income determined by the governing body [of the Legal Aid Board] on the basis of the information submitted by the litigant. If the income data for the reference year that is available deviates from the income data already applied or the amount as per the second sentence, and this has consequences for the assignment of counsel or the sum of the personal contribution owed by the litigant, the governing body shall take a decision ex officio which shall replace the earlier decision. Article 34d(1), third sentence, shall apply.
  2. If on the basis of the decision taken ex officio by the governing body as per the first paragraph the personal contribution owed by the litigant is higher, the extra amount owed is payable to the governing body. If the personal contribution owed is lower or non-existent, the litigant may claim the excess amount back from the governing body. No interest or fees shall be reimbursed over the sums to be paid or claimed. Article 34f shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  3. The assets are the assets in the reference year. The first paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  4. Further rules for the determination of the income and assets as considerations relevant to the litigant's financial capacity may be set by Legislative Decree.
Article 34b shall apply mutatis mutandis to the determination of the income and assets of someone other than the litigant as per Article 34(3).

1. If in the year in which the request for assignment of counsel has been made there is a drop in income or assets, upon the request of the litigant the governing body [of the Legal Aid Board] shall take a decision based on the income or assets in the year in which the request for assignment of counsel has been made. Article 25(3) and (4) shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  2. A drop in income or assets shall be understood to mean a decrease in income or assets of at least 15% relative to the reference year.
  3. The request shall be submitted to the governing body within six weeks of the publication of the decision on the request for assignment of counsel.
  4. The request shall be accompanied by a statement in which the cause of the decrease in income or assets is explained.

1. If the governing body [of the Legal Aid Board] has not denied the request as per Article 34c(1), the governing body shall, if income data over the year in which the request has been made is available which deviates from the income data previously applied or the amount as per Article 34a(1), second sentence, and this has consequences for the assignment of counsel or the sum of the personal contribution owed by the litigant, take a decision ex officio that shall replace the earlier decision as per Article 34c(1), on the understanding that this decision shall not be based on income data higher than that that would be applied in the reference year as per Article 34a(1).
  2. Article 34a(2) shall apply mutatis mutandis.  
  3. By Legislative Decree the cases in which the governing body may decide to assign counsel where the estimated income or assets exceed the limits set out in Article 34(1) and (2), or where the drop in income or assets is less than 15%, may be determined. In those cases the personal contribution of the litigant shall be equal to the highest possible personal contribution set by Legislative Decree as per Article 35(2).

1. Unless otherwise provided by Legislative Decree, a personal contribution shall be payable by the litigant for the provision of legal aid.
  2. The rules on the personal contribution as well as the amount payable shall be set by Legislative Decree.

1. In the cases in which, pursuant to a statutory provision of the Criminal Code or the Code of Criminal Procedure, a suspect, a convicted person or a former suspect has been assigned counsel by the governing body [of the Legal Aid Board], or has been assigned counsel on the instructions of the judge, the legal assistance shall be free of charge, notwithstanding the third paragraph. The first sentence is not applicable to the assistance provided by assigned counsel during questioning as per Article 28d of the Code of Criminal Procedure of a person suspected of a criminal offence in respect of which pre-trial detention is not permitted.
  2. The first paragraph, first sentence, shall apply mutatis mutandis to the legal assistance as meant in: (a) Articles 24(3) and 45a(2) and (3) of the Extradition Act; (b) Article 100 of the Aliens Act 2000; (c) Article 65(1) of the Custodial Institutions (Framework) Act; (d) Article 70(1) of the Young Offenders Institutions (Framework) Act; (e) Articles 52(3) and 64(2) and (3) of the Enforcement of Criminal Judgments (Transfer) Act; (f) Article 1:7(1) and (2) of the Mandtory Mental Healthcare Act; (g) Article 62(1) of the Hospital Orders (Framework) Act; (h) Article 5 of the Temporary Domestic Exclusion Order Act; (i) Articles 38(3) and 56d(6) of the Care and Compulsion (Psychogeriatric and Intellectually Disabled Patients) Act; (j) Articles 24(3) and 43a(2) and (3) of the Surrender of Persons Act; (k) Articles 2:19(6), 2:20(2) and 2:27(5) of the Measures Involving Deprivation of Liberty and Conditional Penalties (Mutual Recognition and Enforcement) Act.
  3. If counsel has been assigned pursuant to Article 39, 40 or 41 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and if the judgment against the convicted person has become final, the governing body may claim the amount of remuneration, as meant in Article 37, from the convicted person whose financial capacity exceeds the amounts provided for in Article 34. With regard to the obligation of the convicted person to pay, Articles 25(3) to (5), 34a, 34b, 34c and 34c shall apply mutatis mutandis, on the understanding that 'the litigant' shall be taken to mean: the convicted person. In the event of failure to pay the full amount the governing body may, after having issued a demand as per Article 4:112 of the General Administrative Law Act, collect the amount by way of a writ of execution within the meaning of Article 4:114 of the General Administrative Law Act.
  4. Further rules regarding the provisions of paragraph 3 may be set by Legislative Decree.

1. If a vulnerable suspect or person suspected of a crime punishable by twelve years' imprisonment or more has been arrested, the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered their detention for investigation at the arraignment shall notify the governing body of the Legal Aid Board of the arrest immediately, in order that the governing body assign a lawyer. This notification need not take place if the suspect has chosen a lawyer and this lawyer or their replacement is available promptly.
  2. If a person suspected of a crime in respect of which pre-trial detention is permitted to have been arrested has, in reply to a question put to him, requested legal assistance, the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered his detention for investigation at the arraignment shall inform the governing body of the Legal Aid Board of the arrest immediately, in order that the governing body assign a lawyer. The second sentence of the first paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  3. If a person suspected of a crime in respect of which pre-trial detention is not permitted to have been arrested has, in reply to a question put to him, requested legal assistance, he shall be given the opportunity to contact a lawyer of his own choice.
  4. If the assigned lawyer is not available within two hours of the notification referred to in the first, second or third paragraph being given, and if the chosen lawyer is not available within two hours of the contact with the suspect pursuant to the first, second and third paragraph, the assistant public prosecutor may, if the suspect waives his right to legal assistance in connection with the questioning, decide to commence the questioning of the suspect.

items.comment: According to the official notification of implementation (see in this regard the comments made above, with respect to Article 1 of the Directive), Article 4(1) to (4) of the Directive finds implementation in Article 12(1) and (2)(a, b and c), in conjunction with Articles 34 to 34d, 35 and 43 of the Legal Aid Act, in conjunction with Article 28b of the Dutch Code of Criminal Procedure. Each of these provisions is set out and translated below.

items.text: 2. Member States may apply a means test, a merits test, or both to determine whether legal aid is to be granted in accordance with paragraph 1.
items.comment: See the comments made above, with respect to Article 4(1) of the Directive.

items.text: 3. Where a Member State applies a means test, it shall take into account all relevant and objective factors, such as the income, capital and family situation of the person concerned, as well as the costs of the assistance of a lawyer and the standard of living in that Member State, in order to determine whether, in accordance with the applicable criteria in that Member State, a suspect or an accused person lacks sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer.
items.comment: See the comments made above, with respect to Article 4(1) of the Directive.

items.text: 4. Where a Member State applies a merits test, it shall take into account the seriousness of the criminal offence, the complexity of the case and the severity of the sanction at stake, in order to determine whether the interests of justice require legal aid to be granted. In any event, the merits test shall be deemed to have been met in the following situations:
items.comment: See the comments made above, with respect to Article 4(1) of the Directive.

items.text: (a)where a suspect or an accused person is brought before a competent court or judge in order to decide on detention at any stage of the proceedings within the scope of this Directive; and
(b)during detention.

5. Member States shall ensure that legal aid is granted without undue delay, and at the latest before questioning by the police, by another law enforcement authority or by a judicial authority, or before the investigative or evidence-gathering acts referred to in point (c) of Article 2(1) are carried out.

provisions.textEn:
1. If a vulnerable suspect or person suspected of a crime punishable by twelve years' imprisonment or more has been arrested, the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered their detention for investigation at the arraignment shall notify the governing body of the Legal Aid Board of the arrest immediately, in order that the governing body assign a lawyer. This notification need not take place if the suspect has chosen a lawyer and this lawyer or their replacement is available promptly.
  2. If a person suspected of a crime in respect of which pre-trial detention is permitted to have been arrested has, in reply to a question put to him, requested legal assistance, the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered his detention for investigation at the arraignment shall inform the governing body of the Legal Aid Board of the arrest immediately, in order that the governing body assign a lawyer. The second sentence of the first paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  3. If a person suspected of a crime in respect of which pre-trial detention is not permitted to have been arrested has, in reply to a question put to him, requested legal assistance, he shall be given the opportunity to contact a lawyer of his own choice.
  4. If the assigned lawyer is not available within two hours of the notification referred to in the first, second or third paragraph being given, and if the chosen lawyer is not available within two hours of the contact with the suspect pursuant to the first, second and third paragraph, the assistant public prosecutor may, if the suspect waives his right to legal assistance in connection with the questioning, decide to commence the questioning of the suspect.

1. The suspect shall have the right to be assisted by defence counsel in accordance with the provisions of this Code.
  2. Legal assistance shall be provided to the suspect in accordance with the manner provided by law, by an assigned defence counsel or defence counsel of his choice.
  3. In special cases and upon reasoned request by the suspect, more than one defence counsel may be assigned.
  4. On each occasion that he requests to speak to his defence counsel, the suspect shall be given the opportunity to do so as much as possible.

items.text: 6. Legal aid shall be granted only for the purposes of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.

provisions.textEn: In the cases in which, pursuant to a statutory provision of the Criminal Code or the Code of Criminal Procedure, a suspect, a convicted person or a former suspect has been assigned counsel by the governing body [of the Legal Aid Board], or has been assigned counsel on the instructions of the judge, the legal assistance shall be free of charge, notwithstanding the third paragraph. The first sentence is not applicable to the assistance provided by assigned counsel during questioning as per Article 28d of the Code of Criminal Procedure of a person suspected of a criminal offence in respect of which pre-trial detention is not permitted.
Persons who pursuant to the Criminal Code or the Code of Criminal Procedure may be assisted by counsel, may be assigned a lawyer by the governing body [of the Legal Aid Board].

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Legal aid in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.text: 1. The executing Member State shall ensure that requested persons have a right to legal aid upon arrest pursuant to a European arrest warrant until they are surrendered, or until the decision not to surrender them becomes final.

provisions.textEn: In the proceedings for surrender of a person by the Netherlands, the requested person has the right to be assisted by a lawyer. Articles 28, 28a, 28c(2), 29a(1), 37, 38, 43 to 45 and 124 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply mutatis mutandis.

If a requested person is arrested pursuant to this statute, the assistant public prosecutor shall notify the governing body of the Legal Aid Board thereof, in order that the governing body appoints a lawyer. Articles 28b(1), second sentence, and 39 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply mutatis mutandis.
The first paragraph, first sentence, shall apply mutatis mutandis to the legal assistance as meant in: [...] (j) Articles 24(3) and 43a(2) and (3) of the Surrender of Persons Act; [...]

items.text: 2. The issuing Member State shall ensure that requested persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution and who exercise their right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10(4) and (5) of Directive 2013/48/EU have the right to legal aid in the issuing Member State for the purpose of such proceedings in the executing Member State, in so far as legal aid is necessary to ensure effective access to justice.

provisions.textEn:
1. Legal aid shall only be granted in respect of legal interests laying in the Dutch legal sphere, to natural or legal persons whose financial capacity does not exceed the amounts set out in Article 34.
  2. Legal aid shall not be granted if: (a) the request for legal aid is evidently devoid of any foundation; (b) the costs related to the legal aid to be granted are not reasonably proportionate to the significance of the case; (c) the request for legal aid relates to a criminal case and it is likely, given the norm to have been violated, that a small fine relative the income will be imposed; (d) the request for legal aid is made by a legal entity established for the purpose of conducting legal proceedings; (e) the legal interest to which the request pertains is self-employment, unless (1) continuance of the profession or company insofar as not in the form of a legal entity is dependent on the outcome of the requested legal aid, or (2) the profession or company has been shut down for at least one year, the applicant is or has been involved in first instance proceedings as a respondent or defendant, and the cost of legal assistance cannot be remunerated any other way; (f) the legal interest is that of bringing the matter before an international body entrusted by treaty with the administration of justice or a comparable international body and the body itself provides for the entitlement of remuneration of legal assistance; (g) the protection of the interest involved can reasonably be left to the applicant, if need be with the assistance of another person or institution whose duties do not fall within the scope of this statute.
  3. Further rules regarding the criteria to be taken into account pursuant to the second paragraph may be set by Legislative Decree.

1. The governing body [of the Legal Aid Board] may deny the assignment if the request: (a) is submitted after the legal aid has in fact already been provided; (b) concerns a legal interest in respect of which the applicant may claim legal aid on the grounds of an assignment previously issued; (c) concerns a legal problem that according to the governing body can be easily settled; (d) concerns a legal problem that can be settled by the facility provided for in article 7(2), or of the facility provided for in article 8(2), insofar as they are charged with the provision of legal assistance.
  2. Further rules regarding the provisions of the first paragraph may be set by the Legislative Decree provided for in article 12(3).
  3. The first paragraph, subparagraphs a and c, shall not apply, where it concerns an assignment in a case in which the legal assistance provided consists of the provision of simple legal advice. The governing body may nevertheless deny a request for assignment, if the request has not been submitted within four weeks of the advice being given.

items.text: 3. The right to legal aid referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 may be subject to a means test in accordance with Article 4(3), which shall apply mutatis mutandis.

provisions.textEn: Legal aid shall only be granted in respect of legal interests laying in the Dutch legal sphere, to natural or legal persons whose financial capacity does not exceed the amounts set out in Article 34.

1. Legal aid as per the provisions of this statute shall be granted to those whose annual income is 21800 Euros [as of 1 January 2020: 27900 Euros] or less if they are a single householder, or, if they share a household with one or more persons, does not exceed 31000 Euros [as of 1 January 2020: 39400 Euros].
  2. In derogation of the provisions of paragraph 1 legal aid shall not be granted, where the litigant's assets exceed their tax-free allowance.
  3. Save in case of mutually contradictory interests, in determining the litigant's income and assets, consideration shall also be given to the income and assets of: (a) the spouse of registered partner of the litigant, unless at the time of the request they are permanently separated; (b) the person of the opposite or same sex with whom the litigant shares a household on a long-term basis, unless at the time of the request there exists between this person and the litigant a blood relationship of the first or second degree.
  4. The income limits as per the first paragraph shall be adjusted each year as of 1 January according to the percentage with which the salary index as of 31 October of the previous year deviates from the corresponding index as of 31 October of the year before that, on the understanding that this shall be rounded off to the nearest multiple of 100 Euros. Each year our Minister shall publish the indexed amounts in the Government Gazette [Staatscourant]. What the salary index, as per the first sentence, comprises, shall be set out in a Legislative Decree.

items.heading: Article 6
items.subHeading: Decisions regarding the granting of legal aid

items.text: 1. Decisions on whether or not to grant legal aid and on the assignment of lawyers shall be made, without undue delay, by a competent authority. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that the competent authority takes its decisions diligently, respecting the rights of the defence.

provisions.textEn:
1. If a vulnerable suspect or person suspected of a crime punishable by twelve years' imprisonment or more has been arrested, the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered their detention for investigation at the arraignment shall notify the governing body of the Legal Aid Board of the arrest immediately, in order that the governing body assign a lawyer. This notification need not take place if the suspect has chosen a lawyer and this lawyer or their replacement is available promptly.
  2. If a person suspected of a crime in respect of which pre-trial detention is permitted to have been arrested has, in reply to a question put to him, requested legal assistance, the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered his detention for investigation at the arraignment shall inform the governing body of the Legal Aid Board of the arrest immediately, in order that the governing body assign a lawyer. The second sentence of the first paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  3. If a person suspected of a crime in respect of which pre-trial detention is not permitted to have been arrested has, in reply to a question put to him, requested legal assistance, he shall be given the opportunity to contact a lawyer of his own choice.
  4. If the assigned lawyer is not available within two hours of the notification referred to in the first, second or third paragraph being given, and if the chosen lawyer is not available within two hours of the contact with the suspect pursuant to the first, second and third paragraph, the assistant public prosecutor may, if the suspect waives his right to legal assistance in connection with the questioning, decide to commence the questioning of the suspect.

provisions.comment:
Own translation; official translation not available.


In other words, this provision is applicable where the requested person has been remanded in custody (taken into bewaring, a form of pre-trial detention; voorlopige hechtenis).
provisions.textEn: If a person deprived of their liberty pursuant to the Surrender of Persons of Act – other than pursuant to a European arrest warrant or a Dutch warrant of arrest or provisional arrest, or an order to be taken into police custody or for such custody to be extended – does not have a lawyer, the governing body of the Legal Aid Board shall, upon notification of the deprivation of liberty by the Public Prosecution Service, appoint a lawyer.

items.text: 2. Member States shall take necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons are informed in writing if their request for legal aid is refused in full or in part.

provisions.comment: Translation borrowed from: https://www.acm.nl/sites/default/files/old_publication/publicaties/15446_dutch-general-administrative-law-act.pdf. Official translation not available.
provisions.textEn:
1. Orders which are addressed to one or more interested parties shall be notified by being sent or issued to these, including the applicant.
  2. If an order cannot be notified in the manner provided in subsection 1, it shall be notified in any other suitable way.

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Quality of legal aid services and training
items.comment: See generally the comments made above, with respect to Article 1 of the Directive, regarding developments in the Dutch legal aid system since 2013.

items.text: 1. Member States shall take necessary measures, including with regard to funding, to ensure that:

provisions.textEn:
The rules to be set by the board with respect to the conditions may relate to:

[...] (b) the expertise of the lawyer in certain areas of the law; [...]

items.comment:
According to the Dutch Government, Article 7(1) to (3) of the Directive finds implementation in Article 15(b) of the Legal Aid Act, in conjunction with the regulations adopted each year by the Legal Aid Board (Raad voor Rechtsbijstand) regarding the conditions under which the legal profession may register with the Board so as to be able provide legal aid services (the 'Inschrijvingsvoorwaarden advocatuur', which are reissued every year), in particular Articles 3 and 6a thereof.


No official translation of the regulations is available, and they are too extensive to translate here. Accordingly, a summary is provided here. These conditions may relate to the organisation of the firm where the lawyer is employed, the reporting by the lawyer with respect to the services provided by them, the minimum and maximum amount of cases in which a lawyer may be assigned and the expertise of the lawyer in certain areas of the law. Article 3 is titled 'Compliance with quality systems agreed on' and should be read in conjunction with Article 15(b) of the Legal Aid Act, while Article 6a is titled 'Expertise requirements for the provision of legal assistance in criminal cases'.

items.text: (a)there is an effective legal aid system that is of an adequate quality; and
(b)legal aid services are of a quality adequate to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, with due respect for the independence of the legal profession.
2. Member States shall ensure that adequate training is provided to staff involved in the decision-making on legal aid in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings.
items.comment: See the comments made above, with respect to Article 7(1) of the Directive.

items.text: 3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of adequate training to lawyers providing legal aid services.
items.comment: See the comments made above, with respect to Article 7(1) of the Directive.

items.text: 4. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have the right, upon their request, to have the lawyer providing legal aid services assigned to them replaced, where the specific circumstances so justify.
items.comment:
According to the Dutch Government, Article 7(4) of the Directive finds implementation in Article 1(l) of the regulations adopted each year by the Legal Aid Board (Raad voor Rechtsbijstand) regarding the conditions under which the legal profession may register with the Board so as to be able provide legal aid services (the 'Inschrijvingsvoorwaarden advocatuur', which are reissued every year).


Article 1(l) of the regulations provides that: In the cases in which he has been assigned the lawyer shall handle it personally and standby duties assigned to the lawyer should be handled by him personally, except in case of force majeure, sickness, hearings in other cases planned on the same day or other compelling reasons. In that case the lawyer shall ensure replacement. In case of replacement, the lawyer assigned shall remain accountable for the quality of the legal assistance provided.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.
items.heading: Article 8

provisions.comment: Translation borrowed from: https://www.acm.nl/sites/default/files/old_publication/publicaties/15446_dutch-general-administrative-law-act.pdf. Unofficial translation; official translation not available.
provisions.textEn:
1. 'Order' means a written decision of an administrative authority constituting a public law act.
  2. 'Administrative decision' means an order which is not of a general nature, including rejection of an application for such a decision.
  3. 'Application' means a request by an interested party for an order.
  4. ‘Policy rule’ means an order, not being a generally binding regulation, which lays down a general rule for weighing interests, determining facts or interpreting statutory regulations in the exercise of a power of an administrative authority.

items.comment:
According to the Dutch Government, this provision finds implementation in Article 1:3 of the General Administrative Law Act, as well as Chapters 6 and 7 thereof.


Article 1:3 of the General Administrative Law Act is set out here, but Chapters 6 and 7 thereof are not, due to their length. Chapters 6 and 7 are titled 'General Provisions Concerning Objections and Appeals' and 'Special Provisions Concerning Objections and Administrative Appeals', respectively. For an impression of these chapters, the user is referred to https://www.acm.nl/sites/default/files/old_publication/publicaties/15446_dutch-general-administrative-law-act.pdf, an unofficial translation of the General Administrative Law Act, with the proviso that this translation may be outdated.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that the particular needs of vulnerable suspects, accused persons and requested persons are taken into account in the implementation of this Directive.
items.heading: Article 9

provisions.textEn: If a vulnerable suspect or person suspected of a crime punishable by twelve years' imprisonment or more has been arrested, the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered their detention for investigation at the arraignment shall notify the governing body of the Legal Aid Board of the arrest immediately, in order that the governing body assign a lawyer. This notification need not take place if the suspect has chosen a lawyer and this lawyer or their replacement is available promptly.

In the cases in which, pursuant to a statutory provision of the Criminal Code or the Code of Criminal Procedure, a suspect, a convicted person or a former suspect has been assigned counsel by the governing body [of the Legal Aid Board], or has been assigned counsel on the instructions of the judge, the legal assistance shall be free of charge, notwithstanding the third paragraph. The first sentence is not applicable to the assistance provided by assigned counsel during questioning as per Article 28d of the Code of Criminal Procedure of a person suspected of a criminal offence in respect of which pre-trial detention is not permitted.
